atoms.b: In AD 900, Scotland was a divided region made up of lots of different ((++kingdoms continents)).
The Vikings tried to invade, but the King of ((++Scotland Spain)), Constantine II, successfully forced them to retreat south.

instruction.text: What do you think Constantine II did to help prevent further Viking invasions?
instruction.sound: What do you think Constantine the second did to help prevent further Viking invasions?

text: In AD 904, Constantine formed the new kingdom of Alba. His army defended Scotland from the Vikings and even took some of Northumbria in AD 918.

instruction.text: In AD 925, Athelstan, the grandson of Alfred the Great, became king of the Anglo-Saxons. How do you think Athelstan felt about the Vikings?

feedback.end: Athelstan wanted to push the Vikings out of England and unite all Anglo-Saxon kingdoms under one ruler. He did this by pushing north into the Danelaw and retaking the important Viking city of York.

b.sound: He didn’t like the Vikings and wanted to take their land.
He liked the Vikings so much that he became one.

instruction.text: With Athelstan pushing the Vikings north and Constantine bringing his army south, what do you think happened to the Vikings?

feedback.end: The Vikings were sandwiched between two powerful rulers, and the pressure from both sides made it hard for them to keep control of the Danelaw.

instruction.text: Find the ruins of the Dunnottar fortress.
instruction.sound: Find the ruins of the Dunnotta fortress.

end.text: In AD 934, Athelstan marched north to take control of Scotland and unite Britain. He attacked Constantine at Dunnottar but couldn’t defeat him.
end.sound: In AD 934, Athel-stan marched north to take control of Scotland and unite Britain. He attacked Constantine at Dunnotta but couldn’t defeat him.

atoms.b: In AD 937, at Brunanburh, ((++Athelstan Alfred)) and Constantine gathered their allies for what turned out to be one of the biggest battles of the time.
Athelstan’s army won, securing his country’s northern borders and ((++retaking losing)) a lot of the land that had once been controlled by the Vikings.
Athelstan is considered to be the first ((++King Queen)) of England.
